review.assessment:
The change replaces a hardcoded tuple check `(st.DONE, st.FAILED)` with `st.is_terminal(job.status)`, ensuring that any terminal status (including CANCELLED) stops the SLA clock at its recorded end time rather than continuing to accrue against current time. This directly fixes the reported issue where cancelled jobs were incorrectly flagged as overdue in the SLA report.

No reproducible defects are present within `sla.py` itself given the provided context and passing acceptance tests. However, the task explicitly requires treating cancelled jobs correctly everywhere it makes a decision based on status, not just in the complained-about report. Since this diff only modifies one file and I do not have visibility into the other five consumers of `job.status`, or the internal implementation of `st.is_terminal`, I cannot verify full spec compliance or provide reproduction commands for unmodified areas. If `CANCELLED` is not explicitly registered as a terminal status in the existing `st` module, this fix will remain latent there.
